summary_hint: a data-vendor property report for a NON-subject property — address, APN, current owner, type/units, assessed & AVM value, tax status — e.g. 'CoreLogic profile, 88 Pine Ave (REO), owner J. Rivera, SFR, assessed $410k, taxes current, non-subject.'

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; the data vendor (source independence)

typed_core.name: data_source
typed_core.why: identity/disambiguator — which dataset the values come from

typed_core.name: report_date
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; report as-of date, drives recency of every value below

typed_core.name: parcel_or_apn
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; the cross-document match key for the parcel

typed_core.name: legal_description
typed_core.why: disambiguator — confirms the APN resolves to the intended parcel

typed_core.name: owner_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — guards a bad owner-name split

typed_core.name: owner_mailing_address
typed_core.why: processor — owner mailing != property address is an owner-occupancy signal

typed_core.name: number_of_units
typed_core.why: processor — CORE; unit count affects financing treatment

typed_core.name: total_assessed_value
typed_core.prompt_hint: Prefer the county/assessor value for total_assessed_value and the vendor AVM for automated_or_reported_value

typed_core.name: assessment_tax_year
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the year the assessed value belongs to (assessed values are stale without it)

typed_core.name: valuation_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the AVM value is meaningless without its as-of date

typed_core.name: subject_property_indicator
typed_core.why: identity — CORE; classifies this as NON-subject
typed_core.prompt_hint: subject_property_indicator is fixed FALSE for this document class, but extract the printed indicator rather than assuming

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — links the profile to the loan file

rejected.name: deed_or_vesting_information
rejected.reason: nested object, no consumer; the title doc is authoritative on vesting

rejected.name: bedrooms / bathrooms / lot_size / construction_or_style
rejected.reason: property detail with no rule and marginal review value on a non-subject property

rejected.name: land_use_or_zoning
rejected.reason: no consumer for a non-subject property

rejected.name: valuation_date_and_confidence (nested)
rejected.reason: flattened to valuation_date; confidence is a conclusion

rejected.name: signature_blocks / notary_block
rejected.reason: a data report is not executed

rejected.name: form_number / form_revision_date / status / effective / expiration / statement period
rejected.reason: not a standardized form; no consumer

encoding_variations: Assessed value vs AVM/market value are different numbers from different sources — assessment_tax_year and valuation_date are the disambiguators that keep them from being conflated
Owner names appear as persons or as an entity (LLC/trust) — captured as flattened strings; the owner_count guards the split
Flood zone may be an FEMA zone letter ('X', 'AE') or prose; capture the code verbatim

open_questions.q: Sales/transfer history and lien summary as nested lists — both genuinely repeat and would be useful to a future prior-transfer or existing-lien rule.
options: build one flat-row list now (which one?)
open_questions.recommendation: defer both to catch-all — no consumer exists, and building bespoke plumbing for a Tier-3 non-subject doc is premature

options: add back for other-real-estate rental income review

notes: No rules read this document today (rule_count 0); there is no rule floor. This profile describes a non-subject property (other real estate owned, comparable, etc.). Fields earn a place by identity, disambiguation, or processor use.
No restricted fields on this doc. Owner names and mailing address are standard sensitivity -> kept as identity fields, not registry PII. No _PII_FIELDS additions.

sales_and_transfer_history and mortgage_lien_or_recorded_document_summary genuinely repeat, but no rule consumes them and each nested list costs ~5 sites of plumbing. Left to the catch-all until a rule needs them.
Prompt hint (doc-level): assessed and market/AVM values are NOT interchangeable — file each to its own field with its date.
